questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the increasing order of metallic character of the elements?

options.explanation: Correct order as metallic character increases down group 2.
This is a correct order but not for the given elements.
These elements are not in the same group.
These are non-metals with decreasing metallic character.

questions.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period. Be, Mg, Ca, Sr are in group 2, so metallic character increases in the order Be < Mg < Ca < Sr.
questions.hint: Metallic character increases down a group.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: The first ionization energy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen due to:

options.explanation: Nitrogen has a lower nuclear charge than oxygen.
Half-filled p-subshell provides extra stability.
Nitrogen has a smaller atomic radius than oxygen, but this is not the primary reason.
Screening effect is not the dominant factor here.

questions.explanation: Nitrogen has a half-filled p-subshell (p³), which is more stable, making it harder to remove an electron. Hence, its first ionization energy is higher than oxygen's.
questions.hint: Consider the electronic configuration stability.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Among the following isoelectronic species, the one with the smallest ionic radius is:

options.explanation: O²⁻ has a lower nuclear charge than Mg²⁺.
F⁻ has a lower nuclear charge than Mg²⁺.
Na⁺ has a lower nuclear charge than Mg²⁺.
Mg²⁺ has the highest nuclear charge, leading to the smallest radius.

questions.explanation: In an isoelectronic series, ionic radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. Mg²⁺ has the highest nuclear charge (+12), so it has the smallest radius.
questions.hint: Ionic radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge in isoelectronic species.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?

options.explanation: Chlorine is less electronegative than fluorine.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity.
Bromine is less electronegative than fluorine.
Iodine is less electronegative than fluorine.

questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table due to its small size and high effective nuclear charge.
questions.hint: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: The correct order of atomic radii for the given elements is:

options.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group.
Atomic radius increases down a group.
Correct order as atomic radius decreases across the period.
Atomic radius increases down a group.

questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge. Na, Mg, Al, Si are in the same period, so the order Na > Mg > Al > Si is correct.
questions.hint: Atomic radius decreases across a period.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the lanthanide contraction?

options.text: It causes the radii of 4d and 5d transition metals to be nearly identical
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about lanthanide contraction.

options.text: It results in Zr and Hf having similar atomic radii
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about lanthanide contraction.

options.text: It increases the basicity of hydroxides down the group
options.explanation: This is incorrect; lanthanide contraction decreases basicity.

options.text: It is due to poor shielding by 4f electrons
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about lanthanide contraction.

questions.explanation: Lanthanide contraction increases the effective nuclear charge, reducing atomic radii and decreasing the basicity of hydroxides down the group. Hence, option C is incorrect.
questions.hint: Lanthanide contraction affects basicity of hydroxides.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: The element with the highest electron affinity among the following is:

options.explanation: Nitrogen has a low electron affinity due to its half-filled p-subshell.
Oxygen has a lower electron affinity than fluorine.
Fluorine has the highest electron affinity.
Neon is a noble gas and has negligible electron affinity.

questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electron affinity due to its high electronegativity and small size, which can accommodate an additional electron effectively.
questions.hint: Fluorine has the highest electron affinity.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: For the given isoelectronic series: N³⁻, O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺, Mg²⁺, the correct order of increasing ionic radius is:

options.explanation: Correct order as ionic radius increases with decreasing nuclear charge.
This is the reverse order.
Incorrect order of Na⁺ and F⁻.
Incorrect order of Na⁺ and Mg²⁺.

questions.explanation: Ionic radius increases with decreasing nuclear charge in an isoelectronic series. The order Mg²⁺ < Na⁺ < F⁻ < O²⁻ < N³⁻ is correct.
questions.hint: Ionic radius increases with decreasing nuclear charge in isoelectronic species.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the diagonal relationship between lithium and magnesium?

options.text: Both have similar atomic radii and form nitrides
options.explanation: Correct explanation for the diagonal relationship.
Magnesium is an alkaline earth metal.

options.text: Both have the same electronic configuration
options.explanation: They have different electronic configurations.

options.text: Both form compounds with similar stoichiometry but different properties
options.explanation: This is not the primary reason for the diagonal relationship.

questions.explanation: Lithium and magnesium exhibit a diagonal relationship due to similar atomic radii and comparable charge densities, leading to similar chemical properties (e.g., both form nitrides).
questions.hint: Diagonal relationship is due to similar atomic radii and charge densities.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Given the following data for ionization energies (in kJ/mol): Element | IE₁ | IE₂ Li | 520 | 7298 Be | 899 | 1757 Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The jump from IE₁ to IE₂ is larger for Be due to its higher nuclear charge
options.explanation: Correct explanation for the larger jump in Be.

options.text: Both elements have similar IE₂ values
options.explanation: IE₂ values are significantly different.

options.text: Li has a higher IE₂ than Be
options.explanation: Li has a higher IE₂, but the jump is not larger.

options.text: The jump from IE₁ to IE₂ is smaller for Be due to its smaller size
options.explanation: The jump is larger for Be due to electronic configuration.

questions.explanation: The jump from IE₁ to IE₂ is larger for Be (1757 - 899 = 858 kJ/mol) than for Li (7298 - 520 = 6778 kJ/mol) because removing the second electron from Be requires breaking the stable 1s² configuration.
questions.hint: Compare the difference between IE₁ and IE₂ for Li and Be.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the increasing order of metallic character of the elements?

options.explanation: Correct order based on periodic trends.
Incorrect order; metallic character decreases from left to right.
Incorrect order; Na has higher metallic character than Mg.
Incorrect order; Si has the lowest metallic character.

questions.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period from left to right. The correct order is Si (Group 14) < Al (Group 13) < Mg (Group 2) < Na (Group 1).
questions.hint: Consider the position of elements in the periodic table and trends in metallic character.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Consider the following ions: P) O²⁻, Q) F⁻, R) Na⁺, S) Mg²⁺. Which of the following arrangements is correct in terms of decreasing ionic radius?

options.explanation: Correct order based on decreasing ionic radius.
Incorrect order; Mg²⁺ has the smallest radius.
Incorrect order; O²⁻ has the largest radius.
Incorrect order; Na⁺ has a larger radius than Mg²⁺.

questions.explanation: In an isoelectronic series, ionic radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. The nuclear charges are: O²⁻ (8), F⁻ (9), Na⁺ (11), Mg²⁺ (12). Hence, the order of radii is O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺.
questions.hint: Isoelectronic ions have the same number of electrons but different nuclear charges.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the diagonal relationship between lithium and magnesium?

options.text: Both form nitrides directly on reaction with nitrogen.
options.explanation: Correct statement about the diagonal relationship.
Electronegativity values are not identical but somewhat close.

options.text: Both form carbonates that decompose on heating to give stable oxides.
options.explanation: This is true for many group 2 elements but not specific to the diagonal relationship.
Atomic radii are not identical.

questions.explanation: Lithium and magnesium show a diagonal relationship. Both form nitrides (Li₃N and Mg₃N₂) directly on reaction with nitrogen. The electronegativity of Li (~1.0) and Mg (~1.2) are somewhat close, but the primary similarity is the formation of nitrides.
questions.hint: Diagonal relationships occur between elements in adjacent groups and periods.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: The first ionization energies (in kJ/mol) of three elements X, Y, and Z are 496, 738, and 577 respectively. If X, Y, and Z belong to the same period, which of the following orders of atomic number is possible?

options.explanation: Incorrect order; Y has the highest IE, so it should have the highest atomic number.
Incorrect order; X should have the lowest atomic number.
Incorrect order; Y should have the highest atomic number.
Correct order based on IE values and atomic numbers.

questions.explanation: The given first ionization energies correspond to Na (496), Mg (738), and Al (577). The atomic numbers are Na (11), Mg (12), and Al (13). Hence, the order of atomic numbers is X < Z < Y.
questions.hint: First ionization energy generally increases across a period, but there are exceptions like between Mg and Al.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following properties of the elements in Group 17 (halogens) shows a **decrease** down the group?

options.explanation: Atomic radius increases down the group.
Electronegativity decreases down the group.
Electron affinity (magnitude) generally decreases but not consistently.
Boiling point increases down the group.

questions.explanation: Electronegativity decreases down Group 17 because the atomic size increases, reducing the attraction for bonding electrons. Atomic radius and boiling point increase, while electron affinity (magnitude) generally decreases but not consistently.
questions.hint: Consider trends in periodic properties down a group.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: The atomic radius of potassium (K) is 231 pm, and that of calcium (Ca) is 197 pm. Using Slater’s rules, estimate the ionic radius of Ca²⁺, assuming the effective nuclear charge (Z_eff) for Ca²⁺ is approximately 2 units higher than for K⁺.

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation.
Incorrect calculation.
Correct calculation based on Slater's rules.
Incorrect calculation.

questions.explanation: - Atomic radius of K = 231 pm → Radius of K⁺ ≈ 231 pm × (1/2)^(1/3) ≈ 183 pm (approximate). - Z_eff for Ca²⁺ is ~2 units higher than for K⁺ → Radius of Ca²⁺ ≈ 183 pm × (1/3)^(1/3) ≈ 136 pm. Hence, the estimated ionic radius of Ca²⁺ is 136 pm.
questions.hint: Slater's rules relate atomic radius to effective nuclear charge and ion charge.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): The second ionization energy of sodium (Na) is higher than its first ionization energy. Reason (R): The second electron is removed from a more stable noble gas configuration.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and R correctly explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: The first IE of Na removes the 3s¹ electron, while the second IE removes an electron from the stable 2p⁶ configuration of Na⁺. Thus, the second IE is significantly higher. Both statements are true, and R correctly explains A.
questions.hint: Consider the electronic configurations of Na and Na⁺.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements is expected to have the **lowest** electron affinity?

options.explanation: Fluorine has a lower electron affinity than chlorine due to repulsion.
Chlorine has the highest electron affinity in Group 17.
Bromine has higher electron affinity than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electron affinity among the given options.

questions.explanation: Electron affinity generally decreases down Group 17 due to increasing atomic size and decreasing effective nuclear charge. Fluorine has a lower electron affinity than chlorine due to its small size and high electron density, which causes repulsion. Thus, iodine, being the largest, has the lowest electron affinity among the given options.
questions.hint: Electron affinity trends down a group in the periodic table.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: The radii of the following ions are given: Na⁺ = 102 pm, Mg²⁺ = 72 pm, Al³⁺ = 53 pm, O²⁻ = 140 pm. If an isoelectronic series is formed by these ions, which ion will have the **smallest** radius?

options.explanation: Na⁺ has a larger radius than Al³⁺.
Mg²⁺ has a larger radius than Al³⁺.
Al³⁺ has the smallest radius due to the highest nuclear charge.
O²⁻ has the largest radius in the series.

questions.explanation: In an isoelectronic series, the radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. The nuclear charges are: Na⁺ (11), Mg²⁺ (12), Al³⁺ (13), O²⁻ (8). Hence, Al³⁺, with the highest nuclear charge, has the smallest radius.
questions.hint: Isoelectronic ions have the same number of electrons but different nuclear charges.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains why the first ionization energy of nitrogen (N) is greater than that of oxygen (O)?

options.text: Nitrogen has a half-filled p-subshell, which is more stable.
options.explanation: Correct explanation for the higher ionization energy of nitrogen.

options.text: Oxygen has a higher atomic number than nitrogen.
options.explanation: Atomic number does not directly explain ionization energy differences.

options.text: Oxygen has a larger atomic radius than nitrogen.
options.explanation: Larger atomic radius usually means lower ionization energy.

options.text: Nitrogen forms a diatomic molecule, while oxygen does not.
options.explanation: Both nitrogen and oxygen form diatomic molecules.

questions.explanation: Nitrogen has a half-filled p-subshell (p³), which is more stable than the p⁴ configuration of oxygen. This stability makes it harder to remove an electron from nitrogen, resulting in a higher first ionization energy.
questions.hint: Consider the electronic configurations of nitrogen and oxygen.
questions.subject: jee-chemistry
